# Deployment checklist for tp.example.test

Generated by the tangra deployment wizard for Teleport 19.1.2.

## Host

- [ ] A Linux host with systemd, at least 2 vCPU and 1 GB of memory (4 GB
      for more than a few dozen users or resources), and `curl` installed.
- [ ] Outbound HTTPS to cdn.teleport.dev (the installer) and to Let's Encrypt (the certificate).

## DNS

- [ ] An A (or AAAA) record for `tp.example.test` pointing to the host's public address.
- [ ] An A (or AAAA) record for `*.tp.example.test` pointing to the same address (application access).

## Network

- [ ] TCP port 443 open to all sources: the web UI, `tsh` and agents all use it.
- [ ] Nothing else listening on port 443 on the host.

## Certificate

- [ ] Port 443 reachable from the internet, so Let's Encrypt can validate
      `tp.example.test` (TLS-ALPN-01). The certificate is requested on first start;
      notices go to ops@example.test.

## Then

1. Run `install.sh` as root next to `teleport.yaml`.
2. Follow `setup-commands.txt`: the first administrator, then the
   `tangra-manager` role and the management identity (and, for portal
   terminals, the `tangra-access` role and its sign-in identity).
3. Run the wizard's prerequisite checks, then register the cluster.
